question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution:
The correct answer is '**following**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage refers to a period of four years leading up to the Boston Tea Party.
 
• The word “following” is commonly used to indicate a period after or leading up to a specific event.
 
• “Following up to the Boston Tea Party” correctly expresses the intended timeframe.
 
• Other options (“trailing,” “lagging,” “leading”) do not fit the grammatical or contextual requirements of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

Complete Passage: *The volume of tea imports into the Colonies rose at a very fast rate in the four years **following__** up to the Boston Tea Party. They went from 55 tonnes in 1770, which was close to the amount dumped in the harbour, to 370 tonnes the year the tea was dumped. This was an increase of almost seven times. The population of the Colonies was about 2 million people in 1770 and didn’t change much in that four-year period. Basic economics tells us this sharp increase in supply without more customers meant the price of tea had to fall.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Trailing: Means following behind, but is not used for time periods in this context.
 
• Lagging: Implies being slow or behind, not suitable here.
 
• Leading: Means going before, which is opposite to the required meaning.
